Credits

Built on other people’s work.

MeshOptimiser stands on open source. Here is every library, font and picture it uses, who made it, and the licence it comes under. Thank you to all of them.

Viewing and picking

  • three.jsThe three.js authors

    The 3D view, on WebGPU or WebGL2.

    MIT
  • three-mesh-bvhGarrett Johnson

    Fast picking and ray tests on very large meshes.

    MIT

Mesh processing

  • meshoptimizerArseny Kapoulkine

    The simplifier behind Decimate and Smart Fit, and Meshopt compression on export (gltfpack too, when it is installed).

    MIT
  • DracoGoogle

    Reads and writes Draco-compressed GLB files.

    Apache 2.0
  • Open Asset Import Library (assimp), as assimpjsThe assimp team; assimpjs by Viktor Kovacs

    Opens other 3D formats in the browser.

    BSD 3-Clause; MIT

Reading CAD

  • CadQuery OCPThe CadQuery contributors

    The Python bindings that read STEP files.

    Apache 2.0
  • Open CASCADE TechnologyOpen Cascade SAS

    The geometry kernel under OCP: it reads and tessellates the CAD surfaces.

    LGPL 2.1 with exception
  • trimeshMichael Dawson-Haggerty

    Meshes and GLB writing in the converter.

    MIT
  • NumPyThe NumPy developers

    The numbers underneath it.

    BSD 3-Clause

Look and feel

  • InterRasmus Andersson and the Inter Project Authors

    The typeface of the app and of this site.

    SIL Open Font License 1.1
  • LucideLucide Contributors

    The icons.

    ISC

The pictures

  • Gearbox AssyKhronos glTF-Sample-Models

    The assembly in the screenshots and the online version: a JT CAD sample, converted by Okino Computer Graphics.

    See the repository

MeshOptimiser itself is MIT licensed. The licence files of the bundled libraries are in the vendor folder of the source. Missing a credit, or one is wrong? Tell me.
